title: Chicken Parm
subtitle: The hall's Italian night spread
description: Italian night at the station. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken breasts, pounded ½ inch

steps.title: Pound and season cutlets
steps.instruction: Place chicken between plastic wrap and pound to an even ½ inch. Pat dry, then season both sides with salt and pepper. Set up a breading station: flour in one pan, beaten eggs in the second, breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan in the third.

steps.title: Bread the cutlets
steps.instruction: Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off excess, dip in egg, then press into breadcrumb-parm mixture until fully coated. Place breaded cutlets on a rack and rest 10 minutes so the coating sets — wet breading falls off in the pan.

steps.title: Pan-fry until golden
steps.instruction: Heat olive oil in large skillets over medium-high until shimmering. Fry cutlets 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and 155°F in the center. Work in batches; transfer to sheet pans lined with racks. Wipe excess oil if needed.

steps.title: Verify cutlet temps before saucing
steps.instruction: Probe the thickest cutlet — target 155°F out of the fry oil; carryover and baking will finish to 165°F under cheese. Any piece below 155°F goes back to the skillet for 2 minutes per side. Drain on racks, not paper-only, so crust stays crisp.

steps.title: Boil pasta and warm sauce
steps.instruction: Boil spaghetti in salted water until al dente; drain and toss with a ladle of marinara. Warm remaining marinara in a saucepan — do not boil hard or it splatters on the line.

steps.title: Top with cheese and bake
steps.instruction: Lay fried cutlets in buttered hotel pans. Spoon marinara over each, then layer mozzarella and provolone. Bake at 425°F 12–15 minutes until cheese bubbles and edges brown. Rest 3 minutes before serving — molten cheese burns rookies.

steps.title: Rest baked cutlets
steps.instruction: Pull hotel pans when cheese bubbles at the edges and cutlets read 165°F at the center. Rest 3 minutes uncovered — molten cheese sets and breading stays crunchy. Keep marinara on low beside the pans.

steps.title: Serve Chicken Parm for the crew
steps.instruction: Plate cutlets with spaghetti and extra marinara on sheet trays. Finish with remaining parmesan and basil. Garlic bread goes on a separate tray so crust stays crisp.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover chicken cutlets — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool chicken cutlets and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Hold sauced pasta separate from cutlets so breading stays crisp.
Broil mozzarella only 1–2 min — watch the hall oven.
Pull chicken at 160°F out of the oil and let carryover hit 165°F under cheese.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool chicken cutlets in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating marinara — thick sauce tightens in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The hall's Italian night spread. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Chicken Parm runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
